reason: Three shutdown hangs and one log flood. (1) After any supervisor restart, verified handoff/recovery rows whose target no longer owns the project were re-advanced every 0.5 s, failing LeaseLost and logging runtime.project_restore.waiting at ERROR forever; the loop now selects verified rows only while their target still owns the project, logs a waiting transfer once per reason, and writes blockers only when they change. (2) SIGTERM or a confirmed shutdown waited without limit for open viewer streams relayed from workers; the stable listener now has a 5 s graceful shutdown bound. (3) A cancellation swallowed below a loop (Python 3.11 wait_for in the SQLAlchemy pool, or a driver error during cancel cleanup) left storage dispatch and chat follow-ups running after their single cancel(); they now stop on a flag and are re-cancelled until done; inside #1024's event-driven follow-up loop the flag is checked before each step and after each pass, and shutdown also wakes the waiter. Selected tests cover each mechanism directly.
exclusions: No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. test_recovery_reconciliation.py spawns real processes; it was run with a per-worktree Python 3.12 venv (nebula resolving to this worktree) and passes in full, as on main. test_runtime_processes.py has 4 failures that are identical on main 936b5d5 (from #1022's StartAborted; fixed separately), so it is not selected. PostgreSQL variants run where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set. Real-Core evidence (SIGTERM with an open /api/v1/work/events stream: >90 s on main, 5.5 s here; restore-waiting flood: ~320/min on main, 0 here on the same database) is in the PR body.
